question: How does Angular help prevent XSS?
shortAnswer: Template binding sanitizes untrusted values; avoid bypassing DomSanitizer except for trusted content.
detailedAnswer: Never build HTML with string concat from user input. Prefer text binding. Audit innerHTML usage.

question: What is CSRF and how do Angular apps mitigate it?
shortAnswer: Cross-site request forgery tricks the browser into sending auth cookies; use tokens/SameSite and careful cookie design.
detailedAnswer: HttpClientXsrfModule reads cookie tokens for mutating requests. Prefer token auth in headers for SPAs when appropriate.

question: Why is bypassSecurityTrustHtml dangerous?
shortAnswer: It disables sanitization—malicious HTML/JS can execute if content isn't fully trusted.
detailedAnswer: Only use for content you control end-to-end. Prefer sanitizing markdown pipelines.

question: Security checklist for an Angular enterprise app?
shortAnswer: Sanitize HTML, secure tokens/storage, HTTPS, CSP, dependency audits, least-privilege API scopes, no secrets in bundles.
detailedAnswer: Treat XSS/CSRF/open redirects seriously. Review interceptors handling auth. Train team on DomSanitizer misuse.
